panels.title: Time since the standby last replied

panels.description: One row per walsender connection visible in `pg_stat_replication`, with `application_name`, `usename`, client address and port, and last replay lag in bytes. This is intentionally the one per-connection panel: physical connection identity is `application_name` plus `client_info`, because two simultaneous senders sharing an application name must remain distinguishable. `state` and `sync_state` are carried as labels, so they appear as columns here. Use this cluster-wide table to identify every physical connection in the graphs; it stays unchanged when the Standby selector changes. The client port, state, and sync state can each start a new series when they change.

WITH q AS (
SELECT labels, t, value
FROM prom_last_over_time(('pgwatch_replication_replay_lag_b'), ([['cluster', '=', '${cluster_name}'], ['node_name', '=', '${node_name}']]),
       (CAST((${__to} - ${__to} % ${__interval_ms}) AS BIGINT)), (CAST((${__to} - ${__to} % ${__interval_ms}) AS BIGINT)), (CAST(${__interval_ms} AS BIGINT)), (CAST(round((${__to} - ${__from}) / 1000.0) * 1000 AS BIGINT)))
)

FROM q
WHERE q.value IS NOT NULL AND isfinite(CAST(q.value AS DOUBLE))
ORDER BY CASE WHEN cardinality(q.labels) = 1 THEN map_values(q.labels)[1] ELSE '{' || array_to_string(list_transform(list_sort(map_keys(q.labels)), lambda k: k || '="' || q.labels[k] || '"'), ', ') || '}' END

Standby-side settings such as `hot_standby_feedback`, `max_standby_streaming_delay`, and `recovery_min_apply_delay` must be read on the standby itself; the per-standby **Hot standby feedback** panel is the only primary-side evidence for feedback. `wal_keep_size` and `max_slot_wal_keep_size` require PostgreSQL 13+; below that version, those rows are absent.
